### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.deps

### Question

My config files are very organized; when I switched from lazy.nvim to mini.deps I kept this. 
init.lua requires plugins/init.lua
This in turn requires plugins/lsp.lua, plugins/treesitter.lua, plugins/tmux.lua, etc.
Each of these files, in turn, uses mini.deps add to load the plugin. These plugins do load, and I can use them in my editing, but only a couple will be included when I update my plugins: treesitter, mini.nvim, and a couple of others. However, plugins I am activly using in my editing won't all update: LSP plugins, for example.

If I open the individual files and :source them, then update, they will be included. I cannot figure out if this means that I am doing something wrong, or if mini.deps is buggy on what it decides to update. Note that the same plugins that won't update will show up as unused when I run DepsClean, again, even if I am activly using them. 

Am I messing up? Is there something I can do to force these all my plugins to update?

comment_data.body:
If plugin is not listed in confirmation buffer during update *and* it is listed in the buffer after `:DepsClean`, then it was previously installed but not (yet) `MiniDeps.add`ed to the current session.

I've just tried [this config](https://github.com/joshsurber/.files/tree/master/nvim/.config/nvim) locally (on `dfcbfa1c334460f1eed86e0b2cbb840d9c2778ae` commit) and it works as expected. The `:DepsClean` is empty after second start (i.e. all plugins that were installed are added) and `:DepsUpdate` lists all installed and added plugins.

The only ones that are not installed are the ones that are [not](https://github.com/joshsurber/.files/blob/dfcbfa1c334460f1eed86e0b2cbb840d9c2778ae/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/plugins/init.lua#L5-L7) [sourced](https://github.com/joshsurber/.files/blob/dfcbfa1c334460f1eed86e0b2cbb840d9c2778ae/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/plugins/init.lua#L11-L12) in 'lua/plugins/init.lua' file.

There are also several `add()` statements for the same plugins, which is redundant. Commenting out the ones `add`ed directly in 'init.lua' still have things work as expected.

Without more information about which plugins are not listed, I can not help much.
